findings.checklist_item: - [ ] State the rollback/back-out for the `--yes` flip (revert the flag) and note the first-pass blast radius, or add a rationale for why an unbounded first-pass link-delete wave is safe given the differ recomputes REMOVE deterministically.
evidence: Plan: 'link create and link delete prompt for confirmation and are run with stdin=subprocess.DEVNULL, so the prompt reads EOF and ACLI reports command cancelled on every pass, forever' — i.e. zero real link mutations happen today

Adding --yes means these deletes will now actually remove links in Jira on the next pass — a real mutation whose blast radius (mass link removal on the first post-change pass) is not bounded by a canary or staged rollout in the plan
findings.finding: The `--yes` change flips link-delete from always-cancelled (zero real mutations) to actually executing deletes against live Jira for the first time, but no staged-rollout or explicit rollback note accompanies this behavior change to a long-running reconciler.
scenarios: First pass after deploy removes all links the differ computed as REMOVE across the whole fleet at once, including any the differ mis-computes
findings.suggested_fix: Add a one-line rollback note (revert the two `--yes` flags) and a sentence bounding first-pass blast radius — e.g. that edit 1's now-visible links_failed accounting plus the existing canary gate the risk.

findings.finding: The plan's justification for the `--yes` non-goal rests on an unresolved/incorrect capability assertion: it claims story 25ae 'proved the installed ACLI rejects --json on those same subcommands — passing an unaccepted flag [--yes] would break every link op', conflating --json with --yes. Prior art in the same codebase shows --yes IS accepted: acli.py:716-726 (`workitem delete`) already passes --yes, added by bug 3256 / the live cfd6 capability probe because without it ACLI 'waits on stdin for confirmation and exits non-zero in non-TTY contexts' — the identical EOF-on-stdin prompt failure the plan attributes to 'command cancelled'. The plan does not consider this directly-relevant prior art before deferring the root-cause fix.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Deliberate non-goal (default decision, not a question)'
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the 25ae-based justification with an explicit reference to bug 3256/cfd6: note that `--yes` is a proven-accepted flag on `workitem delete` and that `link create`/`link delete` currently pass neither `--json` nor `--yes`. Either fold the `--yes` addition into this ticket (it has same-repo prior art, unlike a novel live probe), or, if still deferring, base the deferral on a defensible reason (e.g., link subcommands may differ from workitem delete) rather than the incorrect '--json rejected therefore --yes unaccepted' inference.

findings.finding: The '--yes' non-goal rationale rests on a mis-stated external-capability assertion: it conflates the 25ae `--json` rejection with `--yes`, and treats `--yes` as an unverifiable capability whose use 'would break every link op in the fleet', when the repo already VERIFIES `--yes` acceptance on `jira workitem delete` (acli.py:716-726, added by bug 3256 via the live cfd6 capability probe) for the same EOF-on-stdin confirmation-prompt failure this ticket chases. The `link create`/`link delete` subcommands ARE a distinct surface so a probe is still warranted, but the evidence class is Partially-verified (in-repo prior art on a sibling subcommand), not the total-unknown the plan implies.
findings.location: Approach -> 'Deliberate non-goal (default decision, not a question)'
